items.title: Citizenship application fees have gone up
items.summary:
From 28 August 2026 the fees for New Zealand citizenship products and services increased. The Department of Internal Affairs says the application fee rose by 14.4 per cent.
Citizenship by grant now costs NZ$641 for an adult (16 and over) and NZ$320 for a child (15 and under).
The fee for the citizenship test itself has not been set yet and is expected to be charged separately.

items.title: Official test page: retakes, exemptions and fee
items.summary:
The Government's citizenship test page (last updated 4 August 2026) sets out more of how the test will work.
Retakes: you get up to three attempts. If you do not pass, you wait at least 30 working days and then get up to three more.
Fee: there will likely be a fee for each attempt. The amount is still to be decided.
Exemptions: people under 16, people aged 65 or over, people granted an English language waiver, and people who cannot sit the test because of capacity or a severe medical condition, among others.
Topics listed: the Bill of Rights Act, human rights, voting rights and democratic principles, the system of government, Te Tiriti o Waitangi, some criminal offences, and travelling overseas on a New Zealand passport.
Test locations are not decided yet; the aim is to offer the test throughout New Zealand.

items.title: Citizenship test announced for late 2027
items.summary:
On 6 May 2026 the Department of Internal Affairs announced that most adults applying for citizenship by grant will have to pass a test from late 2027. The exact start date is to be confirmed in 2027.
The test will be sat in person: 20 multiple-choice questions, with 15 correct answers (75 per cent) needed to pass.
People who have already applied, or who apply before the test starts, are not affected.
The Department says it will publish study resources well before the test becomes a requirement.
